question:
A 71-year-old male patient comes to establish primary care after relocating from another state. His
previous medical records from 4 years ago indicate no significant health issues and show normal EKG
and colonoscopy results. He reports generally good health but mentions a one-year history of mild
productive cough with clear sputum and a two-year history of increased urinary frequency and difficulty
initiating urination. He reports no fever, chills, breathing difficulties, painful urination, or blood in urine.
His social history reveals daily consumption of 1-2 beers and a 47-year history of smoking one pack of

cigarettes daily. He denies use of illicit substances. Physical examination reveals no abnormalities.
Which diagnostic test should be performed at this time? Answer Choices: (A) Pulmonary function
testing (B) CT scan of the abdomen and pelvis (C) Spirometry testing (D) Serum prostate specific
antigen (PSA) testing (E) Digital rectal examination (F) Low-dose CT scan for lung cancer screening
(G) Chest X-ray (H) Abdominal ultrasound (I) Colonoscopy (J) Urinalysis with culture
 A. Pulmonary function testing
B. Chest X-ray
C. Urinalysis with culture
D. Serum prostate specific antigen (PSA) testing
E. Spirometry testing
F. Digital rectal examination
G. CT scan of the abdomen and pelvis
H. Low-dose CT scan for lung cancer screening
I. Colonoscopy
J. Abdominal ultrasound
